note: Page 24's diagram settles the B convention the catalogue analysis flagged as open: A spans the rim, B runs from the rim to the UNDERSIDE of the bowl, and 150 is a separate dimension from there to the floor. Overall height is therefore B + 150, and the catalogue publishes no combined figure. The same 150 appears on the Riverside Rise diagram on page 25.

Capacity conflict, unresolved by design. Riverside Base 600 and Riverside Flow 600 are published at the same A and B (60 cm, 60 cm) and at different capacities (169 L and 127 L). 169 L is exactly the plain cylinder volume of those dimensions; 127 L is the volume of a cylinder 60 across and 45 tall, i.e. B minus the 150 legs. Every Flow capacity matches the B-minus-150 reading to within a litre, which contradicts the diagram above. The page prints the published figures and the arithmetic side by side and derives nothing.

note: Riverside Base 300 conflict, now testable. The 400 (40x35, 43 L) and the 600 (60x60, 169 L) are each the plain cylinder volume of their published dimensions to within a litre. The 300 (30x35, 17 L) is not: a plain cylinder would hold 24.7 L. 17 L implies a height of 240 mm, and Jungle Flora's listing gives the Base 300 as 30 x 25 cm. The catalogue's 350 is the only figure in the collection that does not reconcile. The page prints the catalogue unchanged and asks for confirmation; it does not substitute the listing figure.

Cross-collection contradiction, now evidenced from both sides. Riverside Base 600 and Riverside Flow 600 share published A and B (60 cm, 60 cm) and differ in capacity (169 L, 127 L). Riverside Base shows the catalogue using plain cylinder volume; Riverside Flow shows it using A x (B-150) for all four rows; Riverside Rise repeats one figure across three heights. The three pages reduce to a single question about which convention the volumes were computed under.

note: Pixie capacity error, unambiguous. A cube's volume is fixed by one number: 150 mm encloses 3.4 L, 170 encloses 4.9, 200 encloses 8.0, 230 encloses 12.2. The catalogue prints 15, 17, 20 and 23 L -- the A dimension in centimetres with cm swapped for L. Unlike every other capacity problem in this catalogue there is no convention that produces these figures. The page prints the table unchanged and shows the enclosed box volume beside it, labelled as geometry and not as a planting capacity.
Pixie is the only collection with no photograph: no project, interior, detail or scale reference. It appears only on the specification page as two small isolated renders.

FOR THE GARDEN PAGE, not Pixie. Page 26 carries a second footnote under the Garden table: '*Recommended pots: - Nicoli bed pot Clypso Matt 50; Nicoli bed pot Minos Cassetta 45'. So the catalogue names liner pots for Garden by third-party brand and model. The Garden page currently says the tray depth and capacity are unpublished and does not mention liners. Not added unilaterally: it names a third-party manufacturer on a JunglePots page (a commercial decision), and the footnote's ownership is probable rather than certain from the layout. Confirm with the client, then add a liner row to the Garden schedule.

The page therefore removes the schedule, the drawing and the colour picker rather than leaving them empty, and states the absence. What the photograph shows is recorded in a separate disclosure labelled observation, not specification.

NO DRAWING was made for Bar Planter, by decision. Every other page traces the catalogue photograph and checks it against a published dimension; here there is no dimension and the object is half-hidden behind its own planting. A trace would have invented a form.

FINISH RANGE FINDING. Bar Planter is photographed in a red-brown that is none of the four named swatches, and the same unnamed red-brown appears in the Big Ben Tower photography. Across the thirteen pages the catalogue's own photography contains at least dark grey, pale sage green, pale green, beige and this red-brown; two of the five are unnamed. The published four-colour range does not describe what the catalogue shows.
